subject: VPC/on‑prem sizing: scaling cadence, egress caps & procurement next steps
messages:
From: Patrick O'Leary <patrick@acme.ai>

Cc: ops@acme.ai, procurement@acme.ai

Subject: Private cluster sizing — go‑live target Jan 31 (initial asks)

Mina / team,

Thanks again for the product demo last week. We're targeting a Jan 31 pilot for our private VPC deployment and need a short checklist from Redwood to lock procurement and networking. High‑level requirements attached (ACME_privgpu_requirements.xlsx). Key items:

- Expected steady steady state: 150 qps of inference at 95th latency <= 150ms (per request, average token length ~120).
- Peak burst spec: up to 1200 qps for ~6 minutes (hourly bursts during ingestion windows).
- Concurrency profile: many short requests (~1–3 token generation calls) plus occasional long chat-like sessions (~1.2k tokens).
- Egress constraints: our colo link is limited to 6 Gbps outbound (we plan private cross‑connect).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 controls required; we will run customer data through the private cluster.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Baseline GPU count and slab sizing recommendations for the pilot (we prefer committed capacity + burst).
2) Suggestions for admission control / warm pools to meet the 1200 qps burst with our 6Gbps egress cap.
3) Any pre‑signed PO language you need on egress / cross‑connect provisioning timelines.

Can we schedule a 45min handoff tomorrow? If you prefer, loop in the infra leads.

Thanks,
Patrick O'Leary
Head of Infra, Acme AI

Attachment: ACME_privgpu_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Patrick — thanks for the clear brief and the attachment. We're available for a handoff today at 3pm PT; sending a calendar invite now.

Quick, high‑level replies to your three asks so procurement can move in parallel:

1) Baseline recommendation (pilot):
   - Committed slab: 4 x A100‑80GB (or equivalent Ampere nodes) with mixed int8 quantization; expected sustained throughput ~140 qps at target latency for typical chat workloads.
   - Buffer for bursts (burst pool): additional 6 x A100s on reserved burst allocation (hot spare) to absorb the 1200 qps short windows when combined with aggressive batching and KV cache warmup.

2) Admission control & egress strategy:
   - Apply prefix caching + early KV restore to reduce duplicate token computation during bursts.
   - Batching window: dynamic up to 20–25ms to improve throughput without violating 95th latency in steady state.
   - Egress mitigation: compress structured responses, and add token‑level egress accounting — practically we can meet 1200 qps bursts if average token payload stays under ~500 bytes and we reserve a 1 Gbps egress headroom for control traffic.

3) PO / procurement language items we typically need:
   - Committed capacity (monthly GPU hours) and defined burst allowances;
   - Cross‑connect lead time (we require a minimum 14‑day notice to provision dedicated interconnects for private deployments);
   - Acceptance window and performance SLOs for the pilot (we propose a 30‑day acceptance trial with SLO measurement).

I'll bring Jonas (performance/runtime) and Laura (customer ops) to the call to go through topology and timelines. Attaching an initial topology diagram (priv-deploy-topology.png) and will follow with a short mutual action plan doc after the call.

--
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Folks — forwarding Patrick's request and my initial reply. Key items for our internal sizing discussion before the 3pm call:

- Constraint: Acme's colo egress 6 Gbps. They want committed capacity with burst to 1200 qps.
- Workload mix: many short calls + occasional long. Token length variance matters for batching and egress.

My rough thoughts (please reply inline):
A) Slab sizing options (cost vs latency tradeoffs):
   1) Conservative (lower cost): 4 x A100 committed + burst 6 x A100. Requires aggressive batching and will increase tail latency for long sessions.
   2) Steady‑latency (preferred for SLAs): 8 x A100 committed + 2 x A100 burst — smoother tails, simpler admission control.

B) Network plan: we should propose egress shaper per tenant and an envelope that protects the cross‑connect. Consider token payload compression and a per‑request byte budget in the SLA.

C) Warmup & cache strategy: pre‑warm KV for top endpoints; prefetch embeddings for common prompts during burst windows.

D) Operational handoffs: procurement will need clear lead times for cross‑connect (14 days), and ops will need runbook entries for burst failover to hosted fallback model (if private capacity saturates).

Please add numbers (qps per GPU assumption, expected token/sec) and I'll fold into the MAP (mutual action plan).

On call in 30m.

-Mina

Mina / team — notes from the perf side after quick calc (we'll validate in a perf run):

Assumptions:
- A100 80GB sustained token throughput for mixed chat ~480 tokens/sec per GPU with int8 kernels and batched decode at 25ms window.
- Average request 120 tokens => ~4 requests/sec per GPU (steady) => ~160 qps per 8‑GPU slab (steady).
- For burst absorption to 1200 qps for 6 mins, we need ~8 extra GPUs if batching windows can temporarily stretch to 35–40ms and KV cache reduces repeated computation. That assumes modest payload sizes.

Recommendation for MAP (itemized):
1) Pilot SKU: 6 x A100 committed + 6 x burst reserved (hot spares) — gives baseline steady capacity ~240 qps with burst to ~1200 qps with aggressive batching.
2) SLA envelope: define per‑request byte budget; on breach, fall back to hosted small model (with explicit failover path).
3) Egress: a 6 Gbps link will be tight for 1200 qps if average response >4KB. Recommend we add a hard byte cap per minute or require them to upgrade cross‑connect to 8–10Gbps for full headroom.

I'll bring draft perf numbers to the call and propose a perf run with their sample traffic next week.

— Jonas
